# The global market for humanoid robots could reach $38 billion by 2035
Feb 27, 2024

Share

![](https://www.goldmansachs.com/images/migrated/insights/pages/articles/the-global-market-for-humanoid-robots-could-reach-38-billion/800X450.jpg)

![](https://www.goldmansachs.com/images/migrated/insights/pages/articles/the-global-market-for-humanoid-robots-could-reach-38-billion/800X450.jpg)

The worldwide market for humanoid robots is forecast to be bigger than analysts in Goldman Sachs Research expected even [a year ago](https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/articles/humanoid-robots).

The total addressable market for humanoid robots is projected to reach $38 billion by 2035, up more than sixfold from a previous projection of $6 billion, [Goldman Sachs Research analyst Jacqueline Du, head of China Industrial Technology research, writes in the report](https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/goldman-sachs-research/global-automation-humanoid-robot-the-ai-accelerant).

web.description:
## What is the humanoid robot market size?
For 2030, BCC Research's $11 billion is now the only current public forecast with a matching 2025-to-2030 period; MarketsandMarkets' July 2026 revision moved its endpoint to 2035. Above all of that sit the bank scenarios that dominate headlines: Goldman Sachs' $38 billion total addressable market by 2035, and the 2050 projections from Morgan Stanley, Citi and UBS that run from $1.4 trillion to $7 trillion.

- 2030 forecast: $11B (BCC Research); MarketsandMarkets' July 2026 revision now runs 2026 to 2035.
- 2035 scenarios: $15B (Interact Analysis) to $139B (Macquarie), with Goldman Sachs at $38B.

## The trillion-dollar forecasts: what the banks say about 2050
| Bank | Headline scenario | Units | Published |
|-|-|-|-|
| [Goldman Sachs](https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/articles/the-global-market-for-robots-could-reach-38-billion-by-2035) | $38 billion total addressable market by 2035 | 1.4 million units per year by 2035; over 250,000 shipments in the 2030 base case | February 2024 |

## What each forecast is actually measuring
### Goldman Sachs: a 2035 total addressable market scenario
[Goldman Sachs Research](https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/articles/the-global-market-for-robots-could-reach-38-billion-by-2035) projected in February 2024 that the total addressable market could reach $38 billion by 2035.

## Bottom line
Above them, the bank scenarios run from Goldman's $38 billion by 2035 to Morgan Stanley's $4.7 trillion and Citi's $7 trillion by 2050, while the sector's disclosed company revenue in 2025 summed to under $1 billion on about 13,000 shipped robots.

## Frequently asked questions
Frost & Sullivan's assembled-robot-only scope gives the low end, while Future Market Insights' broad bundle of platforms, software and services gives the high end.Is the humanoid robot market really worth $5 trillion? Morgan Stanley's much-quoted figure is a 2050 scenario: $4.7 trillion in humanoid revenue, over $5 trillion including supply chain and services, built on roughly 1 billion robots in use by then. Citi projects $7 trillion and UBS $1.4 to $1.7 trillion for the same year. The market's actual disclosed revenue in 2025 was under $1 billion.How large could the humanoid robot market be by 2030? BCC Research forecasts $11 billion in 2030. MarketsandMarkets' earlier model put 2030 at $15.26 billion, but its July 2026 revision moved to a 2026 base of $5.41 billion and a $50.27 billion endpoint in 2035, leaving BCC as the only current 2025-to-2030 public forecast.How large could the market be by 2035? Published 2035 figures span 9x: Interact Analysis is most conservative at about $15 billion, Goldman Sachs describes a $38 billion total addressable market, MarketsandMarkets' July 2026 revision puts 2035 at $50.27 billion, and Macquarie projects $139 billion. Roughly 13,000 humanoids shipped worldwide in 2025 per an Omdia count cited in an AgiBot release, and consumer-priced models like Unitree's G1 and R1 can genuinely be bought.
